title: Special Array With X Elements Greater Than or Equal X
statement:
You get an array `nums` of non-negative integers. Call an integer `x` a match when the count of values in `nums` that are at least `x` equals `x` itself; `x` need not appear in `nums`.

Return the matching `x`, or `-1` if no integer matches. At most one integer can ever match, so the answer is well defined.
notes:
## Intuition

The brute force tries every `x` from 0 to `nums.length` and counts the values that are at least `x`, which is O(n²). No larger `x` can work, because there are only `n` values to count. After sorting `nums` from largest to smallest, the values that are at least `x` form a prefix, so "exactly `x` of them" means the first `x` values are all at least `x` and the next one (if any) is below `x`. Each candidate is then checked in O(1).

## Approach

1. Sort `nums` in descending order and let `n` be its length.
2. For each `x` from 1 to `n` (`x = 0` never works, since every value is at least 0 and there is at least one value):
   - `enoughBig`: the `x`-th largest value, `nums[x - 1]`, is at least `x`, so at least `x` values qualify.
   - `restSmall`: either there is no next value, or `nums[x]` is below `x`, so no more than `x` qualify.
   - If both hold, return `x`.
3. If no `x` passes, return `-1`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [3, 5]` sorts to `[5, 3]`, `n = 2`. For `x = 1`: `nums[0] = 5 >= 1`, but `nums[1] = 3` is not below 1, so two values qualify, not one. For `x = 2`: `nums[1] = 3 >= 2` and `x === n`, so exactly two values are at least 2; return `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for the sort; the scan is O(n).
- Space: O(1) beyond the sort.

## Pitfalls

- `x` does not have to be a value in `nums`: in `[3, 5]` the answer 2 appears nowhere.
- Checking only `nums[x - 1] >= x` is not enough; `[1, 1]` would wrongly give 1 even though two values are at least 1.
- Sort numerically with a comparator; the default sort orders `[10, 9]` as text.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | number of values |
| `x` | the candidate answer |
| `enoughBig` | at least `x` values are `>= x` |
| `restSmall` | the value after the first `x` (if any) is `< x` |
